items.title: Blondie Announce High Noon, First New Album in Nine Years
items.summary:
Blondie have announced High Noon, their 12th studio album and first set of new material in nine years. BMG will release the record on February 26th, 2027, and it stands as the final recording made by co-founding drummer Clem Burke, who died after the sessions were underway.

The lead single, "Spectral Eyes," is out now. Johnny Marr wrote the track and plays guitar on it, opening the album with the clean guitar lines and quick-landing chorus that have defined the band's pop instincts since the late '70s. Marr is one of several guests across the record, joining Sex Pistols bassist Glen Matlock, Beirut's Zach Condon, and Lucius members Jess Wolfe and Holly Laessig.

Work on High Noon started in New York City in 2022 with producer John Congleton, who had previously helmed the band's 2017 album Pollinator. David Wrench later came aboard for additional production and mixing. As Consequence reported, the band had no way of knowing at the outset that the sessions would become Burke's last with Blondie.

Several songs draw on the group's own history. Chris Stein wrote "Heartbreak Kid" with Johnny Thunders in mind, Matlock contributed "Sleepwalking," and "Little Metal Drummer" revisits a song founding keyboardist Jimmy Destri recorded for his 1981 solo album Heart on a Wall, a version that also featured Debbie Harry and Burke.

"This album is classic Blondie — an amalgamation of all our different influences and eras into something new," Harry said in a statement. "This music feels grounded in the present, shaped by who we are and how we're living now." Stein was blunter: "It's been a long, strange ride, and somehow here we are with another Blondie album. I'm not sure what the fuck I'm supposed to say at this point, except that we're incredibly grateful for all your support over the years."

The 13-track album runs from "Spectral Eyes" through closer "Ah, Sunflower, Weary of Time," and continues the genre-hopping the band has practiced since the beginning, moving between punk, dance music, pop and Latin rhythms. Pre-orders are open now ahead of the February 2027 release.

items.title: Justice Score GTA VI, Share Tame Impala/SZA/King Gizzard Collab “Flower In A Hurricane”
items.summary:
Rockstar Games released the launch trailer for Grand Theft Auto VI and confirmed that French electronic duo Justice composed the game's score. The trailer is set to a new Justice song, "Flower In A Hurricane," which features Tame Impala, SZA, and King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard.

The track is an '80s-style synth-rock anthem built around a dramatic opening riff, with Kevin Parker and SZA singing in harmony across most of its running time. Justice and Tame Impala have worked together before, on "One Night/All Night" and the Grammy-winning "Neverender," both from the duo's 2024 album Hyperdrama. Parker and SZA also recorded unreleased material with Mark Ronson roughly a decade ago.

"Flower In A Hurricane" will appear on GTA VI: The Album, the game's 34-song soundtrack, which arrives alongside the game on November 19. Stereogum noted that other pieces of Justice's score have already surfaced in Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look, a half-hour preview streaming on Netflix.

Whether Rockstar will issue the score separately from the soundtrack album remains unclear. The game will also feature in-game radio stations hosted by a roster of well-known musicians, part of a music rollout that has already previewed a sizable chunk of the soundtrack.

items.title: Hulu’s ‘Durango’ Starring Cooper Hoffman & Kathryn Newton Picked Up To Series; Merritt Wever, Mason Gooding & Abbey Lee Join Cast
items.summary:
Hulu has ordered Durango to series, promoting the Cooper Hoffman and Kathryn Newton project from pilot roughly seven months after greenlighting it. The show comes from Eliza Clark, who previously ran Y: The Last Man.

Hoffman plays Mikey, a ski-bum townie chasing a buzz, opposite Newton as Bunny, a homeschooled runaway waiting tables at a greasy spoon. The two fall in love while running from police, criminals, and Mikey's wife, pursuing their own version of the American dream through a string of bad decisions.

Alongside the series order, Hulu added Merritt Wever, Mason Gooding and Abbey Lee to the cast. Wever plays Joni, a local detective who has spent twenty years in a resort town where the biggest case is usually a stolen ski pass and has now landed something far more interesting. Gooding plays Miles, a sharp-tongued young detective paired with Joni, and Lee plays Irina, Mikey's Russian wife, who is fixated on American pop culture and seeking US citizenship.

Chris Storer, creator of The Bear, has joined as an executive producer. Clark writes and executive produces alongside Media Res' Michael Ellenberg and Christina Malach, and American Light Fixture's Storer, Josh Senior and Tyson Bidner. Jesse Peretz directed and executive produced the pilot, and 20th Television and Media Res produce.

Deadline reported that Durango is one of several pilots Hulu has ordered over the past year, with mixed outcomes. The streamer passed in May on Foster Dade, the YA drama starring Matt Bomer from Greg Berlanti and Bash Doran, while the comedy Lex, from Sean Clements and Paul Simms, is about to begin production. Ryan Coogler's X-Files reboot starring Danielle Deadwyler, ordered to pilot in February, received its own series pickup earlier this week.
